key: Thee, Agni, have the Adityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue. They who love offerings cling to thee at solemn rites: by thee the Gods devour the duly offered food.
s: In the book’s opening hymn, which names Agni as each god in turn, this verse turns to the gods; Sāyaṇa, on 2.1.13, reads them as eating and tasting only through Agni, waiting on him since without him they cannot eat the oblation.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.1.13, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400202 (2024)

evidence.words: त्वन्मुखेनैव भक्षयंति त्वज्जिहयैवास्वादयंतीत्यर्थः । तथा त्वामेव रातिषाचः । रातिर्दान दत्तं हविरादि धनं वा। तेन समवेता देवा अध्वरेषु यज्ञेषु सश्चिरे । सेवंत त्वामेव प्रतीक्षंते विना त्वया स्वेषां हविर्भक्षणायोगात्
evidence.gloss: The meaning is: they eat through thy mouth alone, they taste through thy tongue alone. So too the rātiṣācaḥ (rāti is a gift, the oblation or wealth given; the gods joined with it) attend thee at the adhvaras, the sacrifices: they serve thee and wait for thee alone, since without thee they cannot eat their own oblation.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 2.1.13, at [191,13]). Opened the packet for 2.1: Sāyaṇa on 13 makes the Ādityas (Indra and the rest) take Agni as their mouth, the means of eating and drinking, and the pure gods as their tongue, then states the sense: they eat only through his mouth and taste only through his tongue (tvanmukhenaiva bhakṣayanti tvajjihvayaivāsvādayanti), and at the sacrifices they serve and wait on him alone because without him they cannot eat the oblation (vinā tvayā sveṣāṃ havirbhakṣaṇāyogāt). The sentence paraphrases exactly that and adds nothing. Wilson follows him. Plain sense is faithful: verses 3 to 7 and 11 identify Agni with god after god, and 13 and 14 speak of the gods eating through him; no four words of the key repeated.
